Overview

This cookie notice explains how https://rjmlaird.co.uk uses cookies, local storage, pixels, scripts, device identifiers and related technologies. For simplicity, this notice refers to all of these as “cookies” unless a distinction matters.

Cookies can be set directly by this website, known as first-party cookies, or by another organisation whose service is used on the site, known as third-party cookies.

This notice should be read alongside the privacy notice, which explains how personal information is handled more generally.

What cookies are

Cookies are small text files that a website can store on your device, or read from it, when you visit. They can help a website remember information about your visit, such as a preference you have selected, whether you have seen a notice or how a feature should work.

Similar technologies can include local storage, session storage, pixels, tags, scripts, software-development kits, browser identifiers and device-level information. They can be used for similar purposes, including security, preferences, analytics, embedded content and advertising.

Cookies can be session cookies, which normally expire when you close your browser, or persistent cookies, which remain for a specified period or until you delete them.

How cookies are used

Depending on the features enabled on the site, cookies may be used for the following purposes:

  • Essential operation: maintaining security, preventing abuse, remembering a cookie choice and delivering core website functionality.
  • Preferences: remembering choices such as appearance, language, accessibility or display preferences where those features are available.
  • Analytics: understanding how visitors find and use the site, identifying technical problems and improving content, navigation and performance.
  • Embedded content: loading third-party features such as video, maps, social-media posts, forms, calendars or booking tools.
  • Marketing: measuring advertising, building audiences, limiting repeated adverts or supporting remarketing, only if such tools are used and you make the relevant choice.

The actual technologies used are listed in the cookie inventory. This list must be kept up to date whenever a tool, embed, plugin, tag or service is added, removed or reconfigured.

Your choices and consent

Some cookies are strictly necessary for the website, its security or a service you have specifically requested. These may operate without asking for consent because the site cannot provide the relevant function without them.

Other cookies may require your consent before they are set or read. Where consent is required, optional technologies should not load until you have made a clear positive choice to allow them.

You should be able to accept, reject or manage optional cookie categories with equal ease. Rejecting optional cookies should not prevent you from accessing the ordinary public content of this website.

You can change or withdraw a previous optional-cookie choice at any time using the control below.

Essential technologies

Essential technologies support functions that are necessary for the website to operate, remain secure or deliver a service you specifically request. They may include technologies used for:

  • Remembering your cookie choices
  • Security, fraud prevention and rate limiting
  • Load balancing, network management and website delivery
  • Preventing malicious or automated form submissions
  • Maintaining a requested session or interaction
  • Basic accessibility or display settings necessary to provide the selected service

Essential does not simply mean useful to the website operator. A technology should be treated as essential only where it is genuinely necessary for the relevant service or security function.

Analytics and statistics

Analytics can help show how visitors reach the site, which pages are useful, how content performs and whether technical issues affect use. For example, analytics may measure page views, referral source, device or browser type, broad location, navigation paths, load times and interaction with site content.

Analytics should be configured to minimise data collection, avoid unnecessary identification, avoid advertising and cross-site tracking, restrict access and apply suitable retention settings.

If analytics is used solely for aggregate service improvement and meets all relevant exemption conditions, clear information and an easy opt-out may still be required. If it is also used for advertising, profiling, cross-site tracking or other non-exempt purposes, consent is required before it operates.

Preferences and appearance

Preference technologies may remember choices you make, such as a display theme, contrast setting, text preference, language, layout or other appearance and functionality options.

You can also use browser and operating-system settings to control many appearance and accessibility preferences independently of this website.

Embedded content

Some pages may include content or functionality supplied by third parties, such as video players, maps, social-media posts, calendar tools, forms, newsletters, audio players or booking systems.

Third-party embeds can set their own cookies or access information on your device. Where this is not essential, the embed should not load until you choose to allow the relevant category, or you choose to load that specific embed.

A privacy-friendly alternative may be used where practical. For example, a page can show a preview and a “Load content” button rather than loading an external video or social-media embed automatically.

You can usually access the underlying third-party service directly by following a normal link instead of loading an embedded version.

Marketing and advertising

Marketing technologies may be used to measure advertising, build audiences, track conversions, limit repeated advertising or show more relevant advertising on other platforms.

Third-party services

This website may link to or integrate with independent services. Depending on what is active, these may include:

  • Website hosting, content-delivery and security providers
  • Analytics and consent-management providers
  • Newsletter, email or form providers
  • Booking, calendar and payment providers
  • Video, audio, mapping or document-hosting providers
  • Social-media platforms and external publications

Independent providers are responsible for their own cookies, privacy information, security arrangements and terms. Before using an external service or supplying it with personal information, review its own notices.

Browser controls

Most browsers allow you to view, delete or block cookies through their settings. You can also use private browsing modes, clear site data or configure browser extensions that limit tracking.

Browser controls can affect how websites work. Blocking all cookies may prevent parts of a website from functioning correctly, including sign-in, preference, security, booking or form features.

Browser settings do not necessarily replace the choices available through this website’s cookie-preference control. Where you withdraw consent, optional cookies should be prevented or removed in accordance with the configuration of the relevant consent platform.

Personal information

Some cookies and similar technologies may collect or create information that counts as personal data, for example an online identifier, IP address, cookie ID, device information or browsing activity.

Information about how personal data is collected, used, shared, retained and protected is set out in the privacy notice.

Changes to this notice

This notice may be updated when cookies, similar technologies, suppliers, website features or legal requirements change. The latest version will be published on this page with its revision date.

Where a change materially affects optional technologies or your choices, the cookie banner or preference centre should also be updated before the change is made live.
